title: Compact Autoscale Operator: workflow and compact console deck for Dedicated GPU pools
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design a compact, scannable console deck (top-of-screen panel + detail flyout) for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces health, cost signals, autoscale policy controls, and burst management workflows. The goal is to let operators make safe, auditable changes (canary/burst) and reason about cost versus latency trade-offs without leaving the console. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma screens, interactive prototype for usability testing, microcopy for risk dialogs, and a developer handoff package that includes component specs and accessibility requirements.
goals: Make fleet health and pressure signals easily scannable from a single deck
Enable safe autoscale policy edits with previewed cost/latency impact
Support one-click burst actions with time-bound rollback and audit trail
Provide clear cost-per-token / cost-per-minute and attribution to routes/models
constraints: Data surface limited to metrics already available from telemetry team (p99 latency, queue depth, active jobs, token rate)
Must work in a compact header layout and expanded flyout (desktop only for MVP)
Actions require confirmation and tie into existing RBAC/audit systems (backend dependency ENG-20440)
Avoid adding additional backend telemetry requirements in this phase
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma screens for compact deck + detailed flyout reviewed by PM and ENG
Interactive prototype tested with 6 internal operators; summary notes captured
Design tokens, responsive rules, and accessibility notes included in handoff
Edge-case states documented: degraded pool, underutilized pool, burst active, policy conflict
Microcopy for canary, burst, and rollback dialogs approved by legal and support
design_artifacts: Dev ticket seed: ENG-20789 - UI components and telemetry integration
updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff with PM (Sophie Alvarez) and Eng (Luca Moreno). Agreed scope: compact deck + flyout; no mobile for MVP.
2026-03-02: First wireframes posted to Figma. Feedback: PM asks for clearer cost attribution per route; Eng requests simplified state machine for burst confirmation.
2026-03-05: Mid-fidelity screens completed. Usability session scheduled with 6 operators on 2026-03-08.
2026-03-08: Usability test notes: operators liked single-line health indicators but wanted a predictive indicator for imminent SLO breach. Added optional predictive band in design.
2026-03-09: Engineering review: agreed on telemetry mapping and API surface. ENG will surface projected cost delta from simulated autoscale changes (ENG-20612).
2026-03-10: Design review with legal and security for microcopy. Minor edits to burst dialog wording accepted. PRD updated.
review_feedback: PM (Sophie Alvarez): Add per-route cost allocation and link to Cost Explorer; make rollback time defaults conservative (5 minutes).
Eng (Luca Moreno): Prefer a compact toggle for predictive policy preview to avoid extra calls to telemetry; will return API contract by 2026-03-12.
Design Lead (Evan Park): Ensure color scale for health passes WCAG contrast and add non-color indicators for colorblind users.
Support (Amir Rahman): Add a verbose audit message template for burst actions to help incident triage.
tradeoffs: Kept the MVP to desktop only to iterate faster; mobile UI deferred to next cycle which reduces initial reach but accelerates delivery.
Decided to surface predictive cost delta using a locally computed heuristic rather than waiting for full backend model predictions to avoid blocking ENG-20612.
Included a conservative default for burst duration to minimize customer risk; power users can expand to set custom durations in advanced mode.
testing_notes: Internal usability test (6 participants) revealed confusion around 'burst' vs 'canary' language; changed labels to 'Burst (temporary capacity)' and 'Canary (safe rollouts)'.
Accessibility audit pass: keyboard flows for flyout, aria labels for health badges, focus trap on confirmation dialogs verified.
Performance note: animated sparkline simplified to static mini-chart in compact deck to avoid render overhead in consoles with many pools.

notes_for_engineering: Telemetry mapping: p99_latency -> telemetry.p99_ms, queue_depth -> telemetry.queue_depth, active_jobs -> telemetry.active_jobs
